subject.title: skill_workshop: quarantined proposals are CLI dead-ends (no apply/revise/reject path back)

question: Which recovery transition, if any, should Skill Workshop support for quarantined proposals?
rationale: Quarantine is a safety state produced by explicit operator action or scanner failure, so changing it from terminal to recoverable affects security semantics and public CLI/Gateway/UI behavior.

options.title: Add audited quarantine recovery
options.body: Support a bounded recovery path, such as reject-from-quarantined plus revise-to-pending after a fresh clean scan and audit metadata, across service, CLI, Gateway/tool, UI, docs, and tests.

options.title: Unify with restore semantics
options.body: Wait for the rejected-restore direction to settle and extend the same public restore/reopen model to quarantined proposals only if maintainers want one lifecycle verb.

options.title: Keep quarantine terminal
options.body: Document that quarantined proposals are immutable safety holds and users should recreate clean proposals when they want to proceed.

recommendation.title: Add audited quarantine recovery
recommendation.body: Support a bounded recovery path, such as reject-from-quarantined plus revise-to-pending after a fresh clean scan and audit metadata, across service, CLI, Gateway/tool, UI, docs, and tests.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest current-main history signal for the Skill Workshop lifecycle and public docs is the vincentkoc-authored snapshot commit included in v2026.6.11.
